topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course, welcomes students from multiple disciplines, and establishes the core learning objectives of the lecture.

topics.label: Cellular and Developmental Basis of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops from accumulated genetic alterations that disrupt normal tissue differentiation programs and discuss the histology and culture methods used to study this biology.

topics.label: Tumor Progression, Invasion, and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the functional and histological distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, illustrating how invasive and metastatic phenotypes emerge through stepwise progression.

topics.label: Principles and Exceptions of Tumor Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the naming conventions used to classify neoplasms according to their tissue of origin and malignant potential.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the anatomical obstructions, organ disruption, and systemic complications through which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative Epidemiology and Species Incidence of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distribution and frequency of various tumor types across human populations and other multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Clinical Detection and Cancer Screening Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the clinical rationale, effectiveness, and diagnostic limitations of early detection and screening programs for major tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session by directing students to review the stated learning outcomes in preparation for subsequent practicals and lectures.
